questions.q: Why can't a Deployment safely run a replicated database cluster the same way it runs a stateless web app?
options: Deployments cannot run container images larger than 1GB
Deployment Pods have interchangeable names/IPs and no guaranteed stable storage, but a database replica needs a stable identity and the same storage reattached after restarts
Deployments do not support YAML
Databases cannot run inside containers at all
questions.explain: A Deployment's Pods are deliberately interchangeable. A stateful workload like a database replica needs a stable, predictable identity and its exact storage volume reattached on restart — which is what StatefulSet provides.

questions.q: How are StatefulSet Pods named, compared to Deployment Pods?
options: Identically — both use random suffixes
StatefulSet Pods get predictable ordinal names like catalog-db-0, catalog-db-1; Deployment Pods get random suffixes
StatefulSet Pods have no names at all
StatefulSet names are assigned by the user manually every time
questions.explain: StatefulSet gives each Pod a stable, predictable name based on an ordinal (0, 1, 2, ...), unlike a Deployment's randomly-suffixed Pod names.

questions.q: What does `volumeClaimTemplates` in a StatefulSet actually do?
options: Creates one shared volume that all replicas write to simultaneously
Creates a separate PersistentVolumeClaim per replica, so a recreated Pod reattaches to the same storage it had before
Deletes all storage when a Pod restarts
Only applies to Deployments, not StatefulSets
questions.explain: Each replica gets its own PersistentVolumeClaim (e.g. data-catalog-db-1). When that specific Pod is recreated, it reattaches to its own claim, not a fresh empty volume — the data survives.

questions.q: In what order does a StatefulSet start and stop its Pods by default?
options: All Pods start and stop simultaneously, like a Deployment
In ordinal order for startup (0, then 1, then 2) and reverse order for scale-down/teardown
Randomly, with no guaranteed order
Highest ordinal first for startup, lowest first for teardown
questions.explain: StatefulSet starts Pods in ascending ordinal order, waiting for each to be Running and Ready before starting the next, and tears down in reverse (highest ordinal first) — important when a primary must be up before replicas join.

questions.q: At Northbridge, should the checkout and product-catalog application servers run as a StatefulSet or a Deployment?
options: StatefulSet, because all production workloads should use StatefulSet
Deployment, because they are stateless and interchangeable, with no need for stable identity or per-Pod storage
Neither — they should run as bare Pods
StatefulSet, because they handle customer data
questions.explain: Stateless application servers like checkout and product-catalog don't need stable identity or persistent per-Pod storage, so Deployment is the right fit. StatefulSet is reserved for genuinely stateful workloads like a self-hosted database cluster.
